quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your manager, Ms Mahmoud, asked you to finish the client deck by Thursday. You also have a report due the same day. Frame: Subject: Priorities for Thursday: deck or report? / Greeting: Hi Ms Mahmoud, / Sign-off: Thanks, Wale. Arrange the body so she can decide quickly.
options: I'm happy to start on whichever you choose this afternoon.
I've been asked to finish both the client deck and the finance report by Thursday, and I don't think I can do both well.
Which should I prioritise, or could someone else take one of them?
The deck needs about a day and a half, and the report about two days.
quests.hint: Present the conflict, then what each demands, then ask for the decision.
quests.explanation: A manager can only decide if she sees the trade-off. The estimates make the conflict real, and offering to start straight away shows commitment.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to ask your manager for feedback after your first three months. Put together the email.
options: Subject: Request for feedback after my first three months
I have now been in the role for three months, and I would find it very helpful to hear how you think it is going.
Dear Mr Nowak,

Could we set aside twenty minutes in the next fortnight? I would particularly like your view on my client communication and what I should focus on next.

Kind regards,
Selina Farah
quests.hint: Feedback requests should be specific and time-limited.
quests.explanation: Asking for a set time and naming an area makes the request easier to accept. It shows you want to improve, not just to be praised.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your manager asked you to attend a Saturday event, but you already had plans. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Saturday's open day / Dear Ms Barrett, / Kind regards, Mathias Keller). Arrange the body.
options: I appreciate the opportunity.
I could cover the set-up on Friday afternoon, or attend a later event if that would help.
Thank you for thinking of me for the open day.
Unfortunately I have a family commitment that I cannot move on Saturday.
quests.hint: Appreciate, decline honestly, then propose an alternative contribution.
quests.explanation: A refusal to a manager is more acceptable if it includes another way to contribute. It reflects willingness rather than resistance.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are asking a junior colleague to prepare a first draft. Frame: Subject: First draft of the supplier comparison, due Wednesday / Greeting: Hi Ayaan, / Sign-off: Thanks, Priscilla. Lay out the body.
options: Could you prepare a first draft comparing our three shortlisted suppliers by Wednesday afternoon?
I need it for the leadership meeting on Thursday, so I will review it on Wednesday evening.
Please tell me early if anything is unclear or if the timing is a problem.
The criteria I would like you to cover are price, delivery times and customer references, and last year's version is in the shared folder.
quests.hint: Task, purpose and timeline, scope and resources, then support.
quests.explanation: Delegating clearly means saying what, by when and why. Inviting early questions means problems surface before the deadline.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A team leader delegates event organisation to a volunteer. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Would you lead the summer picnic? / Dear Leonie, / Best wishes, Devon). Arrange the body.
options: Could you let me know by Friday whether you can take this on?
The budget is £400, and you would have a team of four volunteers.
I would like to ask if you would organise this year's summer picnic on 26 July.
I will handle the booking of the park.
quests.hint: Ask before assigning, state resources, request an answer.
quests.explanation: Framing a delegation as a question respects the volunteer's choice. Stating budget and team upfront makes an informed answer possible.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Covering Anil's accounts from 4 August / Dear Shirin, / Kind regards, Kathleen). Arrange the body.
options: Anil will send you handover notes by Friday.
Anil will be on leave from 4 to 22 August, and I would like you to cover his three retail accounts.
Please let me know if you have any concerns.
I know this adds to your workload, so we can move your reporting deadlines to the following week.
quests.hint: Acknowledge the burden and offer support along with the request.
quests.explanation: Recognising extra work and offering a concession shows fairness. Giving the handover date reduces anxiety.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your team is waiting on another team's data. Structure the email that asks for it without sounding critical.
options: Hi Zoran,

Could your team send it by Friday? If that isn't possible, please tell me what date is realistic so that we can adjust our plan.

Thanks for your help,
Monique
We are building the pricing model for the launch, and the regional sales data is the last piece we need.
Subject: Data needed by Friday for the pricing model
quests.hint: Say what you need, why, and give the reader a way to propose another date.
quests.explanation: Explaining the dependency makes the request logical, and the alternative option shows respect for the other team's workload.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Data needed by Friday / Hi Monique, / Best, Zoran). Arrange the body.
options: Thanks for explaining what the data is for.
Would that be workable for your model?
We can't deliver everything by Friday because two regions are still being audited.
We can send the other six regions on Friday and the remaining two by the following Wednesday.
quests.hint: Explain the constraint, offer what you can, ask whether it works.
quests.explanation: A partial commitment with dates is more useful than a plain no. Asking whether it works keeps the conversation collaborative.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Delay to regional sales data: help requested / Dear Ms Petrov, / Kind regards, Monique Laurent). Arrange the body.
options: I have asked twice, and I understand his team is busy.
But the launch on 14 July depends on it.
Could you help us agree a date this week?
I am writing about the regional sales data that Zoran's team agreed to send on 20 June, which we still have not received.
quests.hint: Escalation should be factual and solution-focused.
quests.explanation: Mentioning previous attempts shows you tried to solve it first. Asking for help agreeing a date, not blaming, keeps the relationship intact.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Assemble the email requesting a period of unpaid leave.
options: Dear Ms Mehta,
Subject: Request for unpaid leave from 1 to 31 October

I will complete a handover before I go and remain contactable in emergencies. I would be grateful to know if you need any further information.

Yours sincerely,
Petros Georgiou
I would like to request one month of unpaid leave from 1 October to 31 October to care for a family member abroad.
quests.hint: State the request with dates and reason, and show how work will be covered.
quests.explanation: HR needs dates and a brief reason, and management will be concerned about cover. Mentioning the handover addresses that.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Lay out the email in which an employee returning from sickness asks for a phased return.
options: My doctor has signed me fit to return from 14 July, and I would like to ask about a phased return.

The doctor's note suggests four days a week for the first month. I have attached it, and I am happy to discuss how we can plan my workload.

Kind regards,
Loretta Obi
Subject: Phased return to work after sick leave
Dear Mr Hallam,
quests.hint: Say what you are asking for, the evidence, and your flexibility.
quests.explanation: A sensitive health matter needs only the essentials. Attaching the doctor's note supports the request, and flexibility shows cooperation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the email asking HR to correct a mistake in your payslip.
options: Subject: Payslip query: overtime missing, June

My manager, Ms Hale, approved the hours on 14 June, and her email is attached. Could you please check and correct this in July's pay?

Kind regards,
Damien Rocha
I believe my June payslip does not include eight hours of overtime worked on 12 and 13 June.
Dear HR Team,
quests.hint: Identify the problem exactly, give evidence, request a correction.
quests.explanation: Numbers, dates and approval let HR verify the claim quickly. The reference to July's pay proposes a workable solution.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Confidential: concern about behaviour in team meetings / Dear Ms Whitaker, / Yours sincerely, Hiba Tahir). Arrange the body.
options: Could we arrange a private conversation?
I would like to raise a concern in confidence about a colleague's behaviour in team meetings.
I can give specific dates and examples.
On three occasions in the past month, he has interrupted colleagues and made comments about their ideas that made them uncomfortable.
quests.hint: State that it is confidential, give facts rather than opinions, and request a conversation.
quests.explanation: Facts and dates are more credible than personal opinions. Asking for a private conversation is more constructive than accusing in writing.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Safety concern: loose railing on the loading bay / Dear Mr Adekunle, / Kind regards, Elsa Berglund). Arrange the body.
options: I have put tape across the area.
It moved when I leaned on it, and it could cause a fall if someone trips.
I want to report a loose railing on the west side of the loading bay, which I noticed this morning.
But it needs repair as soon as possible.
quests.hint: The hazard, the risk, what you have done, what is needed.
quests.explanation: Safety issues need precise location and a description of the risk. Explaining the temporary action shows responsibility.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Clarifying my priorities for the next two weeks / Dear Mr Pritchard, / Kind regards, Luana Costa). Arrange the body.
options: I want to make sure I am focusing on the right things during my internship.
But I am not sure which is more important.
At the moment I am working on the website updates and the research summary.
Could you tell me which you would like me to finish first?
quests.hint: Show initiative and ask a specific question.
quests.explanation: Explaining the two tasks helps the supervisor answer briefly. A specific question shows effort instead of general confusion.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your manager has added a new project when you are already at capacity. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: New project for July / Dear Ms Mahlangu, / Best wishes, Fabrizio Neri). Arrange the body.
options: However, I currently have three deadlines in July, and I am concerned that adding this would affect quality.
Could we discuss which task might move, or whether the start date could be August?
I would like to take it on.
Thank you for considering me for the new project.
quests.hint: Show willingness, state the constraint, propose options.
quests.explanation: Starting with willingness prevents the message sounding like a refusal. Presenting the constraint as a quality risk is persuasive and focuses on outcomes.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A colleague repeatedly sends you urgent last-minute requests. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Planning our requests to avoid last-minute work / Hi Rhys, / Thanks for understanding, Pauline). Arrange the body.
options: But the last three requests arrived on the afternoon they were needed.
I'm happy to help with your reports.
If you can give me two working days' notice, I can be sure to do them properly.
For genuinely urgent items, please flag them clearly in the subject.
quests.hint: Willing to help, describe the pattern, propose a rule.
quests.explanation: Describing the pattern with numbers avoids blaming a person. Offering a workable rule for urgent items gives a way forward.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Extended weekend cover / Dear Mr Rasmussen, / Kind regards, Elif Aksoy). Arrange the body.
options: If the company can agree either, I would be glad to help.
So I would need overtime rates or time off in lieu to work weekends.
Thank you for explaining the need for weekend cover in July.
My contract is for weekdays only.
quests.hint: Polite, factual and open to a solution.
quests.explanation: Referring to the contract keeps the reply objective. Offering to help under stated conditions avoids a flat refusal.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Thank you, Support Team / Dear Support Team, / Best wishes, Raquel Domingo). Arrange the body.
options: I want to thank each of you for handling 2,300 customer calls in June, our busiest month in three years.
This was only possible because you covered for one another when colleagues were ill.
Thank you.
Response times stayed under two minutes, and our satisfaction score rose to 94%.
quests.hint: Thank, quote results, name the behaviour that made it possible.
quests.explanation: Specific numbers show the team that their work was noticed. Naming teamwork recognises the behaviour you want to see again.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the email to a manager praising a colleague's work.
options: Dear Mr Sutherland,

When their system failed on Friday evening, she stayed until 9 pm to restore their data, and the client emailed to thank her.

I thought you would want to know.

Kind regards,
Branislav Ilic
Subject: Recognition for Adwoa's work on the Kingsley account
I would like to draw your attention to the work Adwoa has done on the Kingsley account.
quests.hint: Describe the action and the result. Do not exaggerate.
quests.explanation: A short, factual account is more convincing than lavish praise. Ending with 'I thought you would want to know' keeps the tone modest.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email to a supplier thanking them after they solved an urgent problem.
options: Dear Mr Sanchez,
Subject: Thank you for the emergency delivery

Because they arrived before 4 pm, we could print the conference materials on time. We are grateful for your flexibility and will remember it when planning future orders.

Yours sincerely,
Ciara O'Neill
Thank you for arranging the emergency delivery of the printer cartridges on Tuesday afternoon.
quests.hint: Thanks, result, relationship.
quests.explanation: Explaining the effect (conference materials on time) helps the supplier see their impact. A hint of future business is a subtle sign of appreciation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Two departments want the same meeting room on the same day. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Meeting Room A on 10 July: a possible solution / Dear Amrit, / Kind regards, Susannah). Arrange the body.
options: Would that work for you?
Our session needs a room for about two hours.
So we could take 9 to 11, and your team could have 11:30 to 1 pm.
I've seen that both our teams have booked Meeting Room A for the morning of 10 July.
quests.hint: Describe the conflict neutrally, propose a concrete solution, ask.
quests.explanation: Naming the conflict without blame keeps it collaborative. A specific proposal saves both teams from a long thread.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Sales asks Engineering to speed up a feature. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Bringing the reporting feature forward / Hi Jana, / Regards, Terence). Arrange the body.
options: Which would be more useful for the client?
Thanks for explaining why the client is keen to see reporting earlier.
We can deliver a simplified version by 30 July.
But the full feature will need until September to be tested properly.
quests.hint: Acknowledge, state the realistic option, ask a question that helps them choose.
quests.explanation: Offering a simpler version by an earlier date is a compromise, and asking which is more useful invites the other team to participate.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Assemble the email in which a manager asks another department to share a resource fairly.
options: Subject: Sharing the design software licences

I would like to propose a booking calendar so that both teams know when licences are free. Could we speak this week to agree how it should work?

Kind regards,
Wilhelmina Kraus
Dear Mr Oduya,
Our two departments currently share ten licences of the design software, and last month our team was refused access on four days.
quests.hint: Problem, facts, solution proposal, invitation to talk.
quests.explanation: Facts about the problem make the proposal credible. Offering a system instead of complaining is likelier to get a positive response.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have never emailed the company's director before, but you need to bring a problem to her attention. Arrange the email to be concise and respectful.
options:
Since the car park was reduced in May, at least ten staff a day cannot find a space, and some have been late to client appointments.

I would be grateful if this could be considered.

Yours sincerely,
Godwin Ali
Dear Ms Hargreave,
Subject: Staff parking: a concern from the Leeds site
I am writing to raise a concern about staff parking at the Leeds site, on behalf of several colleagues.
quests.hint: Keep it short, state who you speak for, and use evidence.
quests.explanation: Senior people prefer short messages that tell them the issue and the scale. Saying you write on behalf of colleagues shows it is not personal.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are asking a director for ten minutes of career advice. Piece together the email.
options: I work in the finance team and admire the way you moved from analysis to leadership.
Subject: Request for ten minutes of career advice

I would be grateful for ten minutes of your time to ask how you approached that transition. I am happy to meet at any time that suits you.

Yours sincerely,
Amelie Roux
Dear Mr Lindqvist,
quests.hint: Explain why you are choosing him, and ask for a small amount of time.
quests.explanation: A specific, small request is easier to accept. Explaining why you chose him is more personal than a generic request.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the email in which you answer a director's question quickly and offer detail on request.
options: Subject: Re: Cost of the Manchester move

This includes removals, IT set-up and two months' overlap of rent.

I can provide a full breakdown if that would be helpful.

Yours sincerely,
Godwin Ali
The total estimated cost of the Manchester move is £86,000, which is £4,000 under the approved budget.
Dear Ms Hargreave,
quests.hint: Answer first; the details come after.
quests.explanation: A director asks a question because she wants the answer. Giving the figure in the first sentence respects her time, and the breakdown is available on request.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your manager sent an unclear instruction: 'Sort out the supplier issue ASAP.' The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Supplier issue: clarifying what you need / Hi Lorraine, / Best, Adrian). Arrange the body.
options: I want to be sure I understand what you need.
Do you mean the late delivery from Brightway, or the invoice dispute with Corran?
Thanks for your message.
If it is the delivery, I can call them this afternoon; if it's the invoice, I will need the contract.
quests.hint: Show readiness, name the possible meanings, and explain what each would involve.
quests.explanation: A clarifying reply should not just ask 'what do you mean?'. Offering interpretations and next steps for each moves the work forward.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have made a mistake in a report already sent to a client. Arrange the email to your manager.
options: Subject: Correction needed: error in the client report
I have found an error in the Kestrel report I sent yesterday: the total for the North region is £41,000, not £14,000.
Dear Mr Achterberg,

I have corrected the file and drafted a short note to the client, which I would like you to see before I send it. I will also add a second check to my process.

Kind regards,
Esi Boateng
quests.hint: Report the error, the fix, and your plan, before your manager hears elsewhere.
quests.explanation: Managers value early honesty. The email presents the fix, invites approval of the client message and explains prevention.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Put together the reply to a colleague who has asked you to join a committee.
options: Thanks for the invitation; I like the idea of the committee.
Hi Ngozi,

I can join from September, since I'm on a large project until then. Would it be all right if I attended one meeting a month rather than two?

Best wishes,
Ramona
Subject: Re: Invitation to join the wellbeing committee
quests.hint: Interest, condition, request.
quests.explanation: A conditional yes explains what you can offer. Suggesting fewer meetings is a reasonable adjustment, not a refusal.
